chapter: Billie Holiday, Basie leadership and studio work
title: Billie Holiday's encores at the Panther Room, Hampton's band
summary: At the Sherman Hotel in 1941 Royal defied Hampton and brought Billie back for encores, starting a lifelong friendship.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Billie Holiday as the musicians knew her

blocks.x: Well, we came into the Sherman Hotel around, I believe it was 1941. We were one of the first of a group of jazz artists that performed at the Panther Room and that was a room that they served the food on the flaming swords and such things as that, quite an elegant room. So, Lionel Hampton was the featured performer there with his orchestra and he had a supporting act there by the name of Billie Holliday. So, before we -- after we had rehearsals and right before we went into our beginning show that night, Lionel told me, since he was always, always, such a hog for the stage, and always liked to be in front of the audience, he told me, in case they wanted her to do an encore, under no circumstances was I to put her on as an encore performer.

So, since I was standing up in front of the band and I announced her and brought her on the floor and I was the one that was leading the applause when she finished, I thought it no more than right that I should bring her back as many times as she warranted. Since Miss Billie Holliday was one of a kind in her particular type of singing, she warranted several encores, which I proceeded to give to her, for which I was roundly chewed out when I finished the night's performance by my band leader, Mr. Hampton.
I proceeded to, in my own very famous way, to tell him what he could do with his band and his philosophies, but at that
time, I was his first alto saxophone player, as well as his coordinator of his band, so he couldn't very well fire me.
Did that continue for the whole engagement?

I brought her back everytime she was supposed to come back, I brought her back, which I think is only the professional way for it to be done and no one is supposed to hog the show. I don't give a damn who it is.
Was that the first time you ever (inaudible)?
Oh, no, I'd heard her before. By me doing that, we became very, very close friends, Billie and I, and it lasted throughout her lifetime.
